tasks.title: Pottery
tasks.instruction: Fill in the missing letters in the paragraph.
tasks.translation: 陶器是一种古老的工艺，人们在特殊的燃木窑中塑形并烧制粘土，做成实用或装饰物品。早期的陶罐靠手工塑形，在简易窑炉中加热，制出更耐久的陶瓷。随着社会发展，技术日趋精细，不同文化形成各自风格。久而久之，陶器既是实用工艺，也成为重要的艺术与文化表达。世界各地的文化都在制作陶器，反映出各自的艺术传统和功能需求。

passage.t: Pottery is an ancient craft that involves shaping and firing clay in special wood-fired ovens (kilns) to create functional and decorative objects. Early

became more refined, with different cultures creating distinct styles. Over time, pottery evolved into both a practical craft and a significant form of artistic and cultural expression. Pottery has been practiced by cultures worldwide, reflecting their unique artistic traditions and functional needs.

layout.title: University Health and Wellness Conference
layout.body:
Join us on September 20 at Bergsen University for an inspiring day dedicated to your health and well-being!

Why attend?
• Learn practical tips for boosting your energy and increasing your mental focus for more effective studying.
• Chat with wellness professionals who specialize in student health.
• Access free resources to support your mental and physical well-being.

Schedule Highlights:
9:00–10:00 AM  Registration and coffee. Meet speakers and fellow students.
10:00–11:30 AM  Keynote: Dr. Aisha Patel on “The Future of Student Healthcare”
11:30 AM–12:30 PM  Panel: “Mental Health in the Classroom” with David Chen, Sofia Martinez, and Dr. Priya Nair
12:30–1:00 PM  Lunch
1:00–2:00 PM  Panel: “Balancing Academics and Wellness” with Jamal Robinson, Mei Lin, and Elena Petrova
2:00–3:30 PM  Workshop: Nutrition and Fitness Tips for Busy Student Life

Register now: http://www.universitywellness.org
All sessions held in the Butler Wellness Center.

options.A: To provide information on a conference keynote address
options.C: To list events happening at a conference
options.D: To provide information about refreshments at a conference

questions.analysis: 时间表列出 keynote、panel、lunch 和 workshop，目的是列出会议活动。

questions.stem: What is likely true about most of the attendees?

options.A: They will receive free healthcare services at the event.
options.B: They work in the health industry.
options.C: They are visiting from other regions.

questions.analysis: 通篇写 student health、fellow students 和学生学习，多数参加者是学生。

tasks.title: Plant Communication
tasks.translation: 植物会交流这一发现改变了我们对植物行为与生态的理解。传统上，植物被视为被动生物，只对环境变化作出反应，而不是主动与周围互动。但研究表明，植物可以通过土壤发送化学信号。这些信号常由根分泌物（根释放到土壤中的物质）携带，能告知邻近植物有食叶动物或致病因子的威胁。例如，玉米植株遭到毛虫攻击时，会释放特定化学物质警告附近的玉米。作为回应，邻近玉米可能在组织中释放一种对毛虫来说难吃的化学物质 MBOA。植物也用电信号迅速应对环境变化。这些信号在植株内传递，使其调整资源分配。有些植物甚至能通过根探测其他植物的存在，从而改变生长模式以避免直接竞争。尽管有这些发现，植物交流研究仍处于起步阶段。研究人员不断发现植物彼此及与环境互动的新方式。
paras: The discovery that plants use communication has changed our understanding of plant behavior and ecology. Traditionally, plants were considered passive organisms, reacting to environmental change rather than actively engaging with their surroundings. However, studies have shown that plants can send chemical signals through the soil.

These signals, often carried by root exudates (substances released by the plants' roots into the soil), can inform neighboring plants about threats like plant-eating animals or disease-causing agents. For instance, when a corn plant is attacked by caterpillars, it can release specific chemicals that warn nearby corn plants. In response, the neighboring corn plants may release a chemical known as MBOA into their tissues, which makes them less palatable to the caterpillars.

Plants also use electrical signals to respond rapidly to environmental changes. These signals travel through the plant, allowing it to adjust resource allocation. Some plants can even detect the presence of other plants through their roots. This allows them to alter their growth patterns to avoid direct competition.
Despite these discoveries, the study of plant communication is still in its infancy. Researchers are continuously uncovering new ways that plants interact with each other and their environment.

questions.stem: According to the passage, there used to be a mistaken view that plants

options.B: released root exudates only in small amounts
options.C: were not significantly affected by ecological factors
options.D: did not actively interact with other plants

questions.analysis: 旧观点把植物视为被动反应、不主动与周围环境互动的生物。

questions.stem: The word "palatable" in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: less palatable to the caterpillars 指组织变得难吃，最接近 appealing to eat 的反义用法，词义本身是“可口的”。

questions.stem: What happens after a corn plant is attacked by caterpillars?

options.A: Nearby corn plants may produce a chemical that caterpillars find unappealing.
options.B: The attacked plant immediately stops releasing root exudates.
options.C: Caterpillars move to a different species of plant.
options.D: Neighboring plants grow taller to avoid competition.

questions.analysis: 受攻击的玉米发出警告，邻近植株释放 MBOA，使组织对毛虫更难吃。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention electrical signals?

options.A: To argue that chemical signals are less important than scientists once believed
options.B: To show another way plants can respond quickly to changes around them
options.C: To explain how plants detect disease-causing agents in the soil
options.D: To describe how researchers first discovered plant communication

questions.analysis: 作者用电气信号说明植物还能迅速应对环境变化并调整资源分配。

questions.stem: What does the passage imply about research on plant communication?

options.A: It has already explained most ways that plants interact.
options.B: It is no longer considered an important scientific field.
options.C: It is still developing and will likely reveal more findings.
options.D: It focuses only on corn plants and caterpillars.

questions.analysis: 末段 still in its infancy，研究人员仍在不断发现新的互动方式。
